rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's onset is carried by an English adversative and by a verse-initial particle the same row refuses to treat as a divider three times inside the span, and the second-person address that opens mid-span is left undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; both prongs verify and the object, not just the digit, checks out. PRONG 1 (onset argued off the translation layer): the row's onset sentence is the English “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.” (web:Isa.9.1) = oshb:Isa.8.23, and the front verse's Hebrew is never spliced anywhere in the row. That verse in fact opens with the causal particle, כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier), so the adversative carrying the seam has no counterpart token in the bytes (tier-4 translation layer, never boundary evidence). The same verse-initial particle then stands at כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier) and opens oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) — the three internal sites the row expressly declines to read as boundaries — so one particle carries opposite structural weight at the front seam and inside the span, unargued. PRONG 2 (the unity ground is byte-false): 'without a fresh subject or addressee' fails inside the span. A fresh verse-initial nominal subject stands at הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier); the next verse turns to explicit second-person address, הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי ... לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier), continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4, byte tier); and the person does not resume in the birth clause יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד לָ֗נוּ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), which is third person. Both witnesses render the address alike — “You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you” (web:Isa.9.3) = oshb:Isa.9.2. What the row gets right stands: the throne-name run, the doubled ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) with the medial-final-mem ketiv correctly refused as a special-letter seg, the in-span ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), the exegesis note at oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) named as apparatus, and the setumah at oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) under the correct type (tier-3 parashah, single witness). CALIBRATION NOTE: this row and all eight of its neighbours pass every Tier-0 check clean, so this is an evidence-quality defect in a load-bearing field, not a Tier-0 violation — medium, not high.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: (a) replace the English-only onset sentence with a pointed splice of the front verse's opening from oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) at byte tier, and state what distinguishes that verse-initial particle from the three internal sites at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) that the row declines to cut — or drop the particle asymmetry and rest the seam on the scene turn argued from spliced bytes; (b) delete 'without a fresh subject or addressee' and argue the unity on the clause-chaining itself, disclosing the fresh nominal subject at oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) and the second-person address at oshb:Isa.9.2-9.3 (= web:Isa.9.3-9.4) rather than denying them. Field boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) once it is argued. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every onset and unity claim in the rewritten rationale carries a byte-tier pointed splice beside its dual-cited ref, no claim of absent subject or addressee survives where the span's own bytes carry one, every zone-A ref keeps its explicit dual, and the row stays clean on ref-validity, mark and web-quote checks.

rulings.challenge_claim: The fresh-clause onset and the refrain close are byte-clean, but the supporting grammatical-role claim about Ephraim and Samaria is contested in both witnesses, as is its contrast with the preceding unit.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge verifies on the object it names. The onset itself stands and is not contested. What fails is the supporting grammatical-role claim that 'Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit'. The bytes place both names in apposition to the subject of a third-person plural verb: וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.9.8 = web:Isa.9.9, byte tier) — subject-side, neither object nor addressee — and the English agrees, “All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,” (web:Isa.9.9) = oshb:Isa.9.8. I independently re-read every verse of the span, from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12), and confirm no second-person form occurs anywhere in it. The second half of the stated contrast fails too: in the preceding unit the second-person forms at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3) address the giver of the joy, while the royal figure there is third-person throughout, וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), so no addressee is being replaced. Severity holds at low: this is a supporting characterisation, not the row's driver — the fresh verse-initial subject at oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) and the refrain close at oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12) both verify at byte tier, and the refrain is byte-identical at five verses (sweep: 5 verses, byte tier), so the row's digit and its named earliest site are right. No morphology layer is staged; the person and role claims here are argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: replace 'Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria become the addressed object, replacing the royal house of the preceding unit' with the role the bytes carry — an appositional expansion of the subject of the third-person plural verb at oshb:Isa.9.8 (= web:Isa.9.9) — and either drop the contrast with the preceding unit or restate it as a shift of oracle TARGET rather than of addressee. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no grammatical-role label stands unless the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings carry it, and the corrected sentence asserts no second-person form anywhere from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12), which carries none.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the stanza's only stated onset ground - that no fresh subject reopens - is contradicted by a verse-initial explicit subject in its own first verse and a second subject switch in the next, and the single tier-3 signal at this seam falls after that first verse rather than before it. LF: confidence sits at high for a stanza cut inside the 9:7-10:4 refrain poem, a forecast hazard zone, and the jump above the immediately preceding stanza's medium rating is unsupported by stanza-specific evidence.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row and their items are DISTINCT defects, not one defect twice; both verify from bytes and both are upheld as stated. OL's item (evidence): the row's only stated onset ground, that no fresh subject or addressee reopens, is byte-false at the span's own first verse — וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא שָׁ֖ב (oshb:Isa.9.12 = web:Isa.9.13, byte tier) is a verse-initial explicit nominal subject, and it is not the subject of the refrain clause it follows, whose subjects are אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.11 = web:Isa.9.12, byte tier); the very next verse switches subject again at וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Isa.9.13 = web:Isa.9.14, byte tier). The cure is not to reverse the boundary: the same referent already carries the preceding stanza at הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.9.8 = web:Isa.9.9, byte tier), so the discourse continuity the row is reaching for survives — it is the wording that is false, and it understates the row's own front-seam evidence. OL's second prong also verifies: the setumah is keyed AT oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13), i.e. the break falls AFTER this unit's first verse, grouping that verse with what precedes; the row discloses it only as an interior break that does not move the close and never notes that it bears against the front seam it sits beside (tier-3 parashah, single witness, never a driver, absence never counterevidence). LF's item (calibration): confidence sits at high for a stanza cut inside the refrain-poem run that the strategy forecasts as an expected low-confidence region, with the 5:25-bridge rival disclosed and undisposed. NEW FINDING that sharpens LF: across the four-stanza run the confidence banding is INVERTED against onset-signal strength — the two stanzas whose onsets carry no fresh signal at all (this row; and the one opening on a particle continuation at oshb:Isa.9.17 = web:Isa.9.18) are rated high with frontier_flag_considered false, while the two that do carry verse-initial onsets (the divine-word dispatch at oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8 and the woe onset at web:Isa.10.1) are rated medium with the flag true. The weaker-evidence rows are the ones escaping the low-band queue.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field confidence: lower to medium so the band does not exceed the neighbouring stanza's while the same rival is disclosed and undisposed, and set frontier_flag_considered to true with the matching sidecar and frontier-queue rows; if high is kept instead, it must be earned by stanza-specific evidence this stanza's own bytes supply. Field boundary_rationale: replace 'No fresh subject or addressee reopens' with the claim the bytes carry — the verse-initial nominal subject at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13) resumes the same referent already carrying the preceding stanza at oshb:Isa.9.8 (= web:Isa.9.9) — with the pointed splice and the tier named. Field device_notes: add that the setumah keyed at oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13) falls after this unit's own first verse, so as tier-3 single-witness corroboration it bears against this front seam rather than for it. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no 'no fresh subject/addressee' claim survives where the span's first verse opens with one; the mark disclosure states the side the break falls on; the confidence band is not higher than a sibling row resting on strictly stronger onset evidence; mark and ref checks stay clean.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the refrain close and mark disclosure verify, but the seam argument in the rejected alternative places the addressee shift a verse early and calls 'named' a class that neither witness names. LF: confidence sits at high for another stanza cut inside the same refrain poem without a stanza-specific reason for rating above the run's opening stanza.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row; the items are DISTINCT. LF's item is UPHELD AS STATED and OL's is REAL BUT MISFRAMED, so the row verdict is refine. LF (calibration): confidence high for a stanza cut inside the same forecast hazard run, with no stanza-specific ground for rating above the run's opening stanza — and this row's own onset is a particle continuation, כִּֽי בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.9.17 = web:Isa.9.18, byte tier), which the row itself states honestly, so its onset evidence is the weakest in the run while its band is the joint highest; frontier_flag_considered is false here and true on the two medium siblings. OL (seam argument): the corrected finding is that the failing word is 'named', NOT the location of the shift. The following unit's onset supplies no name — ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי אָ֑וֶן (web:Isa.10.1, byte tier) identifies its targets by participial description only, and the English does the same, “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees” (web:Isa.10.1); the sibling row arguing that very target calls it 'the unnamed decree-writers', so two rows in one part describe one seam incompatibly. But OL's supporting arithmetic is wrong: the first second-person forms, וּמַֽה תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ (web:Isa.10.3, byte tier), stand TWO verses after the woe onset, not 'one verse further on'. And the shift itself is not misplaced — the woe cry at web:Isa.10.1 is itself the turn to a new target, after the refrain closes at oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21), exactly as the row says; the row's close and its setumah disclosure at that verse both verify (tier-3, single witness), and the refrain is byte-identical at five verses (sweep: 5 verses, byte tier).
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the word 'named' — the woe target at web:Isa.10.1 is identified by participial description in both witnesses — and keep the shift located at the woe onset, which the bytes do support; the corrected sentence must agree with the sibling row that argues the same target. Field confidence: lower to medium with frontier_flag_considered set true and the matching sidecar and frontier-queue rows, or earn high from this stanza's own bytes, which currently open on a particle continuation. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the corrected sentence survives a both-witness read of web:Isa.10.1, contradicts no sibling row's description of the same target, and any second-person claim names the verse that actually carries the forms (web:Isa.10.3, two verses past the onset).

rulings.challenge_claim: The span contains an undisclosed ketiv/qere site, and every seam claim in the row except the woe onset is argued from the English with no Hebrew form behind it.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge is part real, part misread, so it is refined rather than upheld whole. REFUTED SUB-PRONG: 'Assyria's own boastful self-assessment is not what the span opens with' answers a claim the row does not make — the row says the unit RUNS THROUGH the boast, and the bytes bear that out: the divine first-person forms אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ and אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier) hold web:Isa.10.5-10.7, and the boast then occupies web:Isa.10.8-10.11, inside the span. The row's rejected alternative refers to the further boast quotation at web:Isa.10.13-10.14, which does follow the span, so it is coherent as written. UPHELD SUB-PRONG: the back seam carries no spliced Hebrew at all — the closing boundary rests entirely on the English of the rhetorical question, whose Hebrew reads הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי (web:Isa.10.11, byte tier); under the standing engagement rule a boundary-relevant claim owes its pointed splice. REFRAMED SUB-PRONG: the in-span ketiv/qere site at web:Isa.10.6 is real — one note, staged as the doubled pair ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (web:Isa.10.6, byte tier for the spliced pair; the ketiv member is unpointed and is skeleton grade standing alone) — but no unconditional disclosure debt is owed there: the campaign's unconditional span-relevant symmetry sweep covers petuchah and setumah, while the ketiv/qere arm validates claims that are made, and this row neither counts nor slices in that verse. What is real is within-part inconsistency: the first row of this same stretch discloses its own in-span ketiv/qere site while this one does not. NEW FINDING (stronger than the prong it replaces): the span absorbs an undisclosed tier-1 internal frame — the quotation formula כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (web:Isa.10.8, byte tier), “For he says, “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8) — which is where the speaker changes from divine first person to the Assyrian king's quoted boast; the row names neither the frame nor any speech-formula signal key, though the sibling rows in this stretch are held to disclosing internal seam candidates and arguing why they do not cut. Both setumah disclosures (web:Isa.10.4, web:Isa.10.11) verify under the correct type, tier-3, single witness.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field boundary_rationale: splice the closing verse's pointed Hebrew for the back seam at web:Isa.10.11 at byte tier instead of resting it on the English rendering. Field device_notes: add the internal speech-frame disclosure — the quotation formula at web:Isa.10.8 separates the divine first-person speech of web:Isa.10.5-10.7 from the king's quoted boast at web:Isa.10.8-10.11 — with a stated reason for holding the unit together across it; and add the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.10.6, matching the practice this part already follows elsewhere. Field observed_substrate_signals: add a speech_formula.* key for the quotation frame. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every seam claim in the row carries a byte-tier pointed splice; the internal-frame disclosure states a reason that would equally justify NOT cutting there (a bare mention does not discharge it); mark and ref checks stay clean. This is a disclosure order only — no boundary change is proposed or authorised here.

rulings.challenge_claim: An in-span ketiv/qere site is undisclosed, the 'one uninterrupted response' ground passes over an intervening speech in the other mouth and a change in the divine party's grammatical person, and the closing remnant-object claim is made without a pointed form.
rulings.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the core holds, two supports need correction, so refine. UPHELD: the row's unity ground, that the two therefore-clauses are 'one uninterrupted divine response ... with no addressee change between them', passes over a speech in the other mouth — the quotation frame כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier), “For he has said, “By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.” (web:Isa.10.13) — opening the king's boast between the two clauses; and OL is right that 'no addressee change between them' cannot do the work, since neither clause has an addressee at all, so the stated ground fails to distinguish this seam from any other in the stretch. UPHELD: the closing remnant-object claim in device_notes is asserted with no pointed form, though the verse does carry the plain noun the row names, וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.19, byte tier) — a boundary-relevant claim on that root owes its splice and its tier. CORRECTED: OL's grammatical-person support does not hold as framed. The alternation is already INTERNAL to the first therefore-clause — וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ is third person and אֶפְקֹ֗ד first person in the same verse (web:Isa.10.12, byte tier) — so the third-person stacked title at לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (web:Isa.10.16, byte tier) is not a change ACROSS the clauses and carries no seam weight; if anything it supports the row. CORRECTED: the in-span ketiv/qere site at web:Isa.10.13, staged as the doubled pair ועתידתיהם וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ (web:Isa.10.13, byte tier for the spliced pair), is real, but as at the sibling row no unconditional disclosure debt is owed — the unconditional symmetry sweep is the petuchah/setumah one, the ketiv/qere arm validates claims made, and this row neither counts nor slices there; the finding is within-part inconsistency. NOT CARRYING: the suffixed epithet וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ (web:Isa.10.17, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) is correctly identified as a DIFFERENT object from the title construct in the next unit's first verse, and because the two are different objects the cross-seam cohesion rule does not trigger — it is an observation, not a defect. Both mark disclosures verify with petuchah at web:Isa.10.19 kept distinct from setumah at web:Isa.10.11 (tier-3, single witness).
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'both continue one uninterrupted divine response to the same quoted boast, with no addressee change between them' with a ground the bytes actually distinguish — the quoted boast in the king's mouth opened by the quotation frame at web:Isa.10.13 sits BETWEEN the two therefore-clauses, so the unity must be argued over that quotation rather than by the absence of an addressee neither clause has; do not rest the replacement on a grammatical-person change across the clauses, since the alternation is already internal to web:Isa.10.12. Field device_notes: splice the pointed remnant noun at web:Isa.10.19 with the tier named instead of asserting the object without a form, and add the in-span ketiv/qere note at web:Isa.10.13 for within-part consistency. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the replacement ground must DISTINGUISH this seam from the other seams in this stretch — a ground satisfied equally by every neighbouring cut is no ground — and every remnant claim names its object and its tier before any digit.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: device_notes misassigns web:Isa.10.22 to the plain-common-noun remnant object when its own letter bytes carry the same two-word collocation that constitutes the name-reactivating clause at web:Isa.10.21. OL: the same misassignment, plus the signature divine title in the unit's first verse engaged only through the English, the throne-name collocation spliced but unremarked, and the back-seam frame named without being quoted.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row on the SAME core defect, and both propose the SAME wrong cure, so the row is refined. SHARED CORE (verified, upheld): the row's device_notes groups web:Isa.10.22 with web:Isa.10.20 as 'the plain common noun', but web:Isa.10.22 carries the two-token remnant adjacency שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב (web:Isa.10.22, byte tier), “only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.” (web:Isa.10.22), while web:Isa.10.20 carries the bare construct שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) with no adjacent return-verb at all — so the grouping merges two different objects. CORRECTED CURE (both primaries wrong here): neither 'move web:Isa.10.22 into the clause object' (OL) nor 'it is the identical collocation' (LF) is right. The staged device matrix splits this one adjacency into THREE roles across exactly three verses: the son's name at וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ (web:Isa.7.3, byte tier), the clause REACTIVATING that name at שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier), and the plain clause at web:Isa.10.22 — and it records the name-versus-clause split as live at exactly this seam. TIER CORRECTION (LF): the two runs are NOT byte-identical to each other — the adjacency reaches 3 verses at skeleton and accent-stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses) and web:Isa.10.21 differs from the other two in accents; at BYTE tier the accented run is shared by web:Isa.7.3 and web:Isa.10.22 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), so the sign-name's byte twin is web:Isa.10.22, not web:Isa.10.21. OL's further prongs verify: the signature divine title יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (web:Isa.10.20, byte tier) stands in the unit's own onset verse and is engaged only inside the English quote, with no divine-title object named and no divine_title.* signal key (the bare construct spelling reaches 24 verses at skeleton tier against the staged 25-verse title object, the defective spelling lying outside this stretch); and the spliced אֶל אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר (web:Isa.10.21, byte tier) goes unremarked though the collocation stands at 2 verses at skeleton tier — here and in the throne names at אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), where the accents differ, so that identity is skeleton, not byte. NEW FINDING: the back-seam argument leans on the following unit's divine-word formula, כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (web:Isa.10.24, byte tier), yet web:Isa.10.24 is neither quoted nor present in boundary_evidence_refs — the row argues a verse outside its span that it never names at all.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: re-cut the remnant-object split to the three roles the staged device matrix carries on this one adjacency — the son's name at web:Isa.7.3, the name-reactivating clause at web:Isa.10.21, and the plain clause at web:Isa.10.22 — and reserve 'plain common noun' for web:Isa.10.20's bare construct, which carries no adjacent return-verb; name the recurrence tier explicitly (3 verses at skeleton tier; the accented run shared by web:Isa.7.3 and web:Isa.10.22 at byte tier). Also in device_notes: name the divine-title object standing at web:Isa.10.20 with its pointed splice rather than leaving it inside the English quote. Field observed_substrate_signals: add a divine_title.* key. Field boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Isa.10.24, and quote the frame the back seam leans on with a pointed splice in boundary_rationale. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): every remnant claim names its object BEFORE any digit, no two of the four objects on this root are merged, the three-way split is not collapsed to two in either direction, every recurrence claim carries its tier, and the ref-mirror stays clean with the back-seam verse present.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the unit's own quoted closing verse is missing from its evidence-reference list, an internal citation gap unlike every other row in this stretch. OL: the messenger frame is correctly owned, but both seams sit on byte-true devices left undisclosed - the divine title stack repeats at byte tier from the verse immediately before the front seam, and the span's own closing verse opens with the in-that-day formula this same stretch elsewhere treats as a unit-opening driver.
rulings.grounds: Both primaries hit this row with DISTINCT defects; both verify and both are upheld, OL's strengthened by my own re-derivation. LF (citation completeness): the row quotes its own argued close, “It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.” (web:Isa.10.27), but boundary_evidence_refs stops at web:Isa.10.23 and web:Isa.10.24.
